answers.q1_what_did_you_play: Rapid Fire first, spending the whole 3-Spark bank on the most expensive attack in hand so the 2-cost is the one that gets discounted to 0. With one enemy on the board all four random 4-damage hits land on Nibbit, so that is 16 damage and Pyro for free. That left both energy intact. Kaboom! then costs its printed 1 (the Spark is gone) for 7 more, taking Nibbit from 40 to 17. The last energy went into Duck and Cover for 5 Block, which turns the telegraphed 12 into 7 and leaves me at 35/62.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: Yes. The real alternative was leading Eager to Help while the bank still read 3, so it draws 2 instead of 1, then Rapid Fire free and Kaboom! for the last energy. Same 23 damage, plus two extra cards. I rejected it because after that sequence I am at 0 energy, so the two cards are only useful if they happen to cost 0, and I would eat the full 12 instead of 7. I also weighed spending the Spark on Kaboom! instead of Rapid Fire, but that discounts a 1-cost rather than a 2-cost and costs me a whole card's worth of play this turn.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: Card draw and whatever it would have set up for next turn — Eager to Help stays stranded in hand, and with the Spark bank empty it will only draw 1 whenever I do play it, so the 2-card version of that card is gone for now. It also gives up nothing on damage, since 23 was the ceiling either way; what it buys with the last energy is 5 HP of mitigation rather than information.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. Duck and Cover is only there because of the 12-damage attack. If Nibbit had telegraphed a buff, a debuff, or anything non-damaging, the last energy would have gone to Eager to Help instead — and in that case I would have played Eager to Help first, before Rapid Fire, so the Spark bank was still at 3 and it drew 2 rather than 1. A much larger incoming number would not have changed the line either; 5 Block is still the best use of the final energy, it just matters less.
